# Implementation Plan: Lifecycle-first sync-on-read + staleness guard for `overview.parallel_ready_tasks`
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"ralph-overview-mcp-snapshot-sync-on-read"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

*Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/ralph-overview-snapshot-freshness/selected-direction.md` (D-001).*

## Overview

The ralph-overview MCP tool `overview.parallel_ready_tasks` builds its ready-task
candidates from a possibly-stale generated `snapshot.json` and filters them on the
Ralph **stage** only — it never consults the authoritative task **lifecycle** in
`.ralph-overview/data.json`. The result is the 2026-06-06 incident: the tool returned
40 "ready" tasks of which 28 were already `merged`/`archived`, and it omitted same-day
filings that were absent from the stale snapshot.

This plan makes the read path **lifecycle-first**: read `data.json` fresh per call as the
authoritative task-set + lifecycle spine, hard-exclude `merged`/`archived` independent of
Ralph stage, include same-day filings absent from the snapshot (using their `initialStage`
+ `command.prompts` kickoff), overlay the snapshot's Ralph stage + dependency data as
**enrichment only**, and surface `snapshotAgeMs` + a human-readable stale reason. It reuses
existing infrastructure (`SnapshotReader.getOverviewData()`, the already-computed
`snapshotStaleSince`, and `WatcherSupervisor`). Full sync-on-read is explicitly rejected on
latency grounds (~17s/call); D-002 (hardening the background watcher) stays out of scope.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
- **`tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/parallel-ready-tasks.ts`** is the single behavioral surface.
  - `parallelReadyTasks()` (102-140) builds candidates from `snapshot.tasks.filter(isCandidateStage)` (119) and a prereq map `tasksById` from `snapshot.tasks` (114).
  - `isCandidateStage()` (162-168) computes `stage = task.ralph?.stage ?? task.initialStage` and excludes only on `EXCLUDED_STAGES = {shipped, replan-pending, blocked}` (22). **It never checks `task.lifecycle` — this is the root bug.**
  - `computeSnapshotStaleSince()` (338-354) ALREADY computes whether `data.json`/job-state is newer than the snapshot; the result is attached as advisory `snapshotStaleSince` (132-135) but never surfaced as an age/reason.
  - Missing-snapshot today is a **hard fail** (`{ok:false, error:'missing snapshot'}`, 108-110).
  - `ParallelReadyTasksResult` (74-81) has **no enforced output schema** (schemas.ts only constrains `watcher_status` output) → new result fields are additive / non-breaking.
- **`tools/overview-mcp/src/snapshot-reader.ts`**: `getOverviewData()` (84-98) returns fresh
  `OverviewData` via `loadOverviewData(dataFile)`, cached in `#overviewData` and invalidated
  only by the in-process chokidar watcher in `start()` (36-58). It has no mtime self-guard today.
- **Reference pattern — `tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/expand-task-context.ts`** (76-95): calls
  `getOverviewData()`, reads `overviewData.tasks`, finds the task by id, then overlays
  `getSnapshot()` + `resolveStage()` as enrichment. This is the exact lifecycle-first + snapshot-
  overlay shape D-001 wants. **(Seed correction: `unblock-candidates.ts` does NOT read data.json
  lifecycle — it filters the snapshot's derived `task.unblockCandidate` flag. It is snapshot-only,
  not the reference pattern.)**
- **Types** (`tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts`, re-exported by `overview-mcp/src/types.ts`):
  `OverviewTask` (42-61) = `{id, scope?, lifecycle?(string), phase?(@deprecated alias), status?,
  initialStage?(RalphStage), blockedOn?(string[]), command?(prompts{brainstorm,plan,impl}), ...}`.
  **`SnapshotTask extends OverviewTask { ralph?: RalphPipelineState; unblockCandidate?: boolean }`**
  (345-348) — a snapshot task IS an overview task plus `ralph`, which is exactly why stale
  lifecycle leaks through the snapshot. `DependencyGraph` (330-343) edges run dependent→prerequisite
  (`blocks` = blocked→blocker). `NextCommand` (324-328) = `{label, command, icon?}`.
- **`scripts/lib/derive-next-command.mjs`**: `deriveNextCommand(state, task, opts)`; when `state`
  (ralph) is absent it derives a kickoff from `task.initialStage` + `command.prompts`
  (97-127) → a snapshot-absent data.json task still yields a kickoff command.
- **Tests**: `__tests__/parallel-ready-tasks.test.ts` + `__tests__/helpers.ts` already provide
  `writeOverviewData()` (writes data.json), `writeSnapshot()`, `setMtime()`, `makeContext()`,
  `taskIds()`, `readyTask()` — everything needed to build a fresh-data.json / stale-snapshot fixture.

### Technical Constraints
- **Architecture invariant (plugin AGENTS.md):** lifecycle is the bookkeeper-authoritative axis;
  the snapshot/job-state-derived stage + dependency fields are an enrichment layer. This plan
  must keep that split — it does not move stage derivation onto the read path.
- **Performance:** `data.json` parse must stay sub-second; no full job-state walk / sync on the
  read path. `getOverviewData()` is already cached, so a parse happens at most once per `data.json`
  change, not per call.
- **No snapshot-schema change:** we do not add fields to `RalphPipelineState`/`SnapshotTask`/the
  generated snapshot, so `scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.mjs` and its Ajv regression are untouched.
- **Result-envelope additions are non-breaking** (no output Zod schema on this tool); existing
  consumers reading `readyTasks`/`snapshotStaleSince`/`watcherFailure` keep working.
- **Build/test:** plugin-root `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (Vitest runs
  `--no-file-parallelism --maxWorkers=1` on Windows). The overview-mcp workspace has its own
  `build`/`typecheck`/`test` scripts.

## Approach

### Architecture
Pivot `parallelReadyTasks()` so the **authoritative task-set + lifecycle** come from
`getOverviewData()` (data.json), and the snapshot supplies **enrichment** (`ralph` stage,
artifacts, dependency graph, PRD-derived story gating) overlaid by task id. Data flow:

```
getOverviewData() ── overview.tasks (authoritative: id, lifecycle, initialStage,
        │                              command.prompts, blockedOn, status)
        ▼
  for each task: merge with snapshot task by id  → mergedTask (SnapshotTask shape)
        │            (overlay ONLY ralph + unblockCandidate from snapshot)
        ▼
  HARD lifecycle gate: drop lifecycle ∈ {merged, archived}      ← THE FIX
        ▼
  stage gate: stage = ralph?.stage ?? initialStage; drop EXCLUDED_STAGES; apply stageFilter
        ▼
  readiness: lifecycle-aware prerequisite satisfaction (data.json blockedOn ∪ snapshot graph edges)
        ▼
  result: readyTasks[] (+ per-task enrichment marker) + snapshotAgeMs + snapshotStaleReason
```

Because `SnapshotTask extends OverviewTask`, the merged object `{ ...overviewTask, ralph,
unblockCandidate }` is itself a valid `SnapshotTask`, so `toReadyTask()`,
`deriveNextCommand()`, and the stage helpers continue to operate with minimal change.

### Key design decisions (for reviewer scrutiny)

**D-A — Guaranteed freshness via an mtime guard on `getOverviewData()`.**
Make `SnapshotReader.getOverviewData()` record the `dataFile` mtime at load and re-read when the
current mtime differs, so freshness does NOT silently depend on the in-process chokidar watcher
having started or being alive. This strengthens every caller (also `expand-task-context`) and is
deterministic under the test `setMtime()` helper.
- *Alternative considered:* a separate `getOverviewDataFresh()` that bypasses the cache — rejected
  to avoid two near-identical accessors; the mtime guard keeps the single cached method correct.
- *Alternative considered:* read `data.json` raw every call via `loadOverviewData()` — rejected as
  needlessly re-parsing on repeated calls within one `data.json` generation.

**D-B — Merge/overlay helper.**
Add `mergeOverviewWithSnapshot(overviewTasks, snapshotTasks)` returning a `SnapshotTask[]` where
each entry is `{ ...overviewTask, ralph: snap?.ralph, unblockCandidate: snap?.unblockCandidate }`.
Authoritative fields (lifecycle, initialStage, command, blockedOn, status, scope) come from
data.json; only `ralph` + `unblockCandidate` come from the snapshot. Tasks present only in the
snapshot but absent from data.json are **dropped** (data.json is the authoritative task-set).

**D-C — Lifecycle hard gate.**
Add `EXCLUDED_LIFECYCLES = new Set(['merged','archived'])`; the lifecycle gate runs BEFORE the
stage gate and is independent of Ralph stage. `getOverviewData()` → `loadOverviewData()` already
normalizes `lifecycle` (sync-core.mjs `normalizeOverviewTask` 868-886, mapping legacy `phase`
`shipped→merged`/`closed→archived`/`plan-ready→tracked`) and derives `initialStage` from
`command.prompts` when unauthored, so same-day filings with only `command.prompts` still yield a
kickoff via `initialStage`.
- **Lifecycle read — typecheck constraint (review finding, consensus High).** The cleanest read of
  the authoritative base is `task.lifecycle` directly, because `getOverviewData()` already returns it
  normalized — this needs **no new import** and avoids a typecheck failure. The alias-safe helper
  `resolveTaskLifecycle(task)` exists in `scripts/lib/task-aliases.mjs`, BUT that module has **no
  `scripts/lib/task-aliases.d.mts` declaration** (verified: only `derive-next-command`,
  `load-prds-by-task-id`, `derive-dependency-graph`, `sync-core`, etc. have `.d.mts` files), so the
  TypeScript MCP package cannot import it without `npm run typecheck` failing. **Primary approach:**
  read `task.lifecycle` directly against the normalized data.json base + define
  `EXCLUDED_LIFECYCLES`. **Only if** the implementer wants the defensive alias semantics for legacy
  `phase`, they MUST first add a one-line `scripts/lib/task-aliases.d.mts` declaration (mirroring the
  existing sibling `.d.mts` files) in the same story — do not import `task-aliases.mjs` from TS
  without it.

**D-D — Per-task enrichment marker.**
Add an additive optional field to `ReadyTask`, `enrichment?: 'synced' | 'awaiting-sync'`
(`'awaiting-sync'` when the task has no matching snapshot entry, i.e. a same-day filing whose
dynamic stage/dependency fields are not yet watcher-derived). Field name is reviewer-tunable;
it must be additive (no output schema to break).

**D-E — Authoritative readiness via a freshly-derived dependency graph.**
Instead of unioning `blockedOn` with the (possibly stale) `snapshot.dependencyGraph`, **rebuild the
dependency graph fresh from authoritative inputs** using the existing
`deriveDependencyGraph({ byTaskId, overviewData, prdsByTaskId })`
(`scripts/lib/derive-dependency-graph.mjs`, which HAS a `.d.mts` declaration). Argument shapes
(verified against `derive-dependency-graph.d.mts`):
- `overviewData` = the fresh data.json `OverviewData` (its `tasks[].blockedOn` / `tasks[].blocks` /
  `spawnedFrom` drive the `blocks` + `spawn` edges; verified at derive-dependency-graph.mjs:56-70).
- `prdsByTaskId` = the loaded PRDs (drive `depends-on-story` + PRD-root `depends-on-task` edges).
- `byTaskId` = **`Record<string, RalphPipelineState>`** (the helper reads `byTaskId[taskId]?.stage`,
  d.mts type `OverviewRalphState['byTaskId']`) — build it from the snapshot as
  `Object.fromEntries(snapshot.tasks.flatMap(t => t.ralph ? [[t.id, t.ralph]] : []))`. **Do NOT pass
  the merged `Map<string, SnapshotTask>` here** — that fails typecheck and loses stage enrichment
  (`SnapshotTask.stage` is undefined; stage lives under `.ralph.stage`). Keep the merged
  `Map<string, SnapshotTask>` separate for readiness/title lookups.

This single call handles **`blockedOn`, the reverse `blocks` direction, PRD `depends-on-story`,
PRD-root `depends-on-task`, and `spawn`** uniformly from authoritative data — closing the gap where a
data.json-only `blocks`/`blockedOn` relationship (absent from a stale/missing snapshot) would
otherwise let a blocked task surface as ready (review finding, High). Readiness then runs the existing
`taskPrerequisitesSatisfied`/`storyPrerequisitesSatisfied` logic against the FRESH graph, resolving
each task prerequisite `P` as satisfied iff `P.lifecycle==='merged'` **OR** `P.ralph?.stage==='shipped'`
(looked up in the merged `tasksById`) — so a prerequisite that is actually `merged` but stale-staged
in the snapshot no longer wrongly blocks its dependent. Story gating (`isStorySatisfied`) is
unchanged; a snapshot-absent task with no PRD has no open stories → conservatively ready w.r.t.
stories (awaiting-sync).
- **Constraint:** `deriveDependencyGraph` is pure in-memory over its three arguments and does NOT walk
  `.ralph/jobs/*/job-state.json` (verified — derives only from `byTaskId`/`overviewData`/`prdsByTaskId`),
  satisfying the sub-second / no-full-sync budget. Preserve the existing readiness invariants: edge
  `from`→`to` is dependent→prerequisite, and `spawn` edges never block readiness (plugin AGENTS.md
  invariant #11).
- *Rejected alternative:* manual `blockedOn ∪ snapshot.dependencyGraph` union — more error-prone, and
  it ignores data.json `blocks` and inherits stale snapshot edges (review finding, Simplicity/High).

**D-H — Single data.json parse per call (no double-parse).**
`loadPrdsByTaskId({ repoRoot, config, overviewData })` already accepts an `overviewData` argument
(load-prds-by-task-id.mjs:16,23) and falls back to its own `loadOverviewData()` when omitted —
which `parallel-ready-tasks.ts` relies on today, parsing data.json a second time. Pass the
already-loaded `overviewData` from `getOverviewData()` into `loadPrdsByTaskId(...)` so a single
parse feeds both the candidate set and PRD matching (avoids a torn-read where the two parses see
different data.json generations). Adjust `loadMemoizedPrds` to key its memo on the data.json mtime
(or the overviewData identity) in addition to the snapshot mtime.

**D-F — Graceful missing/empty snapshot.**
When `data.json` is present but the snapshot is missing/unreadable, do NOT hard-fail. Proceed with
an empty enrichment set: every task is `enrichment:'awaiting-sync'`, `snapshotAgeMs` is `null`, and
`snapshotStaleReason` says the snapshot is missing. Only when `data.json` itself is absent return
`{ok:false, error:'missing .ralph-overview/data.json'}` (mirroring `expand-task-context`). This
delivers a lifecycle-correct task list even when the watcher never ran — the strongest form of the
fix.

**D-G — Staleness surfacing.**
Add `snapshotAgeMs?: number | null` (= `Date.now() - snapshotMtimeMs`; **`null` when the snapshot is
missing** — the type is `number | null`, not `number`, to match the missing-snapshot AC) and
`snapshotStaleReason?: string`. The reason string MUST (a) include the snapshot age, and (b)
distinguish the two cases with a stable, machine-greppable marker: `data.json newer than snapshot`
(e.g. `"snapshot 42m old; data.json changed 3m ago — Ralph stage/dependency fields may be stale"`)
vs `snapshot missing` (e.g. `"snapshot.json missing — all dynamic fields awaiting sync"`). Keep the
existing `snapshotStaleSince`. Reuse `computeSnapshotStaleSince`'s mtime comparison; do not re-walk
job-state beyond what it already does.

**D-I — Freshness boundary (mtime-guard scope).**
Only `getOverviewData()` (data.json / lifecycle) is mtime-guarded — that is the authoritative
correctness surface. `getSnapshot()` is deliberately NOT mtime-guarded here: snapshot freshness
stays watcher-dependent (the D-002 boundary), and any staleness is *surfaced* via `snapshotAgeMs` +
`snapshotStaleReason` rather than silently masked. Document this boundary so a future reader does not
mistake the snapshot enrichment for a fresh read.

### Open questions resolved (from the brainstorm)
- *data.json newer than snapshot →* return lifecycle-correct results **with a surfaced warning**
  (never fail closed). The point is to stop silently planning from stale lifecycle, not to block planning.
- *Ever return merged/archived? →* **No**, made a tested invariant with stale-snapshot fixtures.
- *Minimal readiness for new tasks →* data.json `blockedOn` AND reverse `blocks` are authoritative
  (re-derived fresh via `deriveDependencyGraph`) even for snapshot-absent tasks; only PRD-`depends-on-story`
  readiness is "awaiting-sync" when the task has no PRD yet. Kickoff via `initialStage` + `command.prompts`.
- *Elevate staleness from advisory →* surface `snapshotAgeMs` + `snapshotStaleReason` as structured
  fields and update the tool `description` to state lifecycle-authoritative + staleness semantics.

### Implementation Strategy (ordered)
1. **US-001** Authoritative lifecycle-first candidate construction (merge helper, lifecycle gate,
   `isCandidateStage` operating on merged tasks, graceful missing-snapshot) + the mtime-guarded
   `getOverviewData()`.
2. **US-002** Same-day-filing inclusion + authoritative readiness via a freshly-derived dependency
   graph (`deriveDependencyGraph` over fresh data.json + PRDs; handles `blockedOn` + reverse
   `blocks`), lifecycle-aware prerequisite satisfaction, `enrichment` marker, `deriveNextCommand`
   kickoff.
3. **US-003** Staleness surfacing (`snapshotAgeMs: number | null` + `snapshotStaleReason`) + tool
   `description` update.
4. **US-004** Version bump to 2.10.0 (plugin.json + 3 marketplace indexes + CHANGELOG) + plugin
   `AGENTS.md` `v2.10.0 Behavioral Additions` docs + root codexu `AGENTS.md` Active Plugin Versions
   table bump + submodule pointer commit (see Repo & Submodule Workflow).

(Tests are written as part of each functional story's acceptance criteria — see Acceptance Criteria
and the per-story outline.)

## Scope

### In Scope
- Lifecycle-first authoritative read of `data.json` per call in `overview.parallel_ready_tasks`.
- HARD exclusion of `lifecycle ∈ {merged, archived}` independent of Ralph stage (tested invariant).
- Inclusion of same-day-filed `tracked` tasks absent from the snapshot, with `initialStage`/prompts
  kickoff and an `enrichment:'awaiting-sync'` marker.
- Snapshot Ralph stage overlaid as enrichment only; **dependency/story readiness re-derived fresh**
  from authoritative data.json + PRDs via `deriveDependencyGraph` (handles `blockedOn` + reverse
  `blocks` + PRD `depends-on-story`).
- Lifecycle-aware prerequisite satisfaction (a prerequisite counts as satisfied when its data.json
  lifecycle is `merged` OR its snapshot Ralph stage is `shipped`).
- `snapshotAgeMs` (`number | null`) + `snapshotStaleReason` surfaced in the result; existing
  `snapshotStaleSince` kept.
- mtime-guarded `getOverviewData()` so freshness does not depend on the in-process watcher.
- Graceful missing/empty snapshot (return data.json-driven candidates, all awaiting-sync).
- Tests for every behavior above; existing readiness/dependency/story tests stay green.
- Version bump to 2.10.0 (plugin.json + 3 toolkit-root marketplace indexes + CHANGELOG) + plugin
  `AGENTS.md` docs + root codexu `AGENTS.md` Active Plugin Versions table + submodule pointer commit.

### Out of Scope
- Full sync-on-read (rejected — ~17s/call).
- D-002 `WatcherSupervisor` cold-start hardening / watcher ownership re-architecture.
- D-003 sync-on-write hooks.
- Changing how the heavy job-state-derived stage/dependency fields are produced by the watcher.
- Touching tools beyond `overview.parallel_ready_tasks` (except the shared
  `getOverviewData()` freshness improvement, which is strictly additive for other callers).
- Any snapshot/`RalphPipelineState` schema change.

## Risk Areas
- **Existing-test regressions from the fresh-graph readiness model.** Replacing the snapshot
  dependency graph with a freshly-derived one (and adding lifecycle-`merged` satisfaction) can change
  outcomes for tests that relied on the snapshot-only `stage==='shipped'` prereq check or on
  snapshot-baked graph edges. Mitigation: run the full `parallel-ready-tasks.test.ts` suite; adjust
  only fixtures that omitted blocker lifecycle / authoritative `blockedOn`; keep assertions intact
  (AC7). Confirm `deriveDependencyGraph` preserves edge orientation and the `spawn`-never-blocks rule.
- **`deriveDependencyGraph` must be pure in-memory.** Verify it derives only from its
  `{byTaskId, overviewData, prdsByTaskId}` arguments and performs NO `.ralph/jobs/*` job-state walk —
  otherwise the no-full-sync / sub-second budget (AC9) is violated.
- **`tasksById` now built from the merged (data.json) set.** A prerequisite present only in the
  snapshot but absent from data.json would no longer resolve; this is correct (data.json is
  authoritative) but must be covered by a test so it is an intentional, documented behavior.
- **Freshness vs. caching.** The mtime guard must compare against the resolved absolute `dataFile`
  path and tolerate a missing file (ENOENT → treat as absent). Avoid a per-call `fs.stat` storm:
  one stat per call is fine (sub-ms); do not stat job-state here.
- **Performance assertion flakiness.** A wall-clock `< 1s` test is environment-sensitive. Prefer a
  structural assertion (data.json parsed at most once per call; no job-state walk) plus a generous
  timing bound on a large synthetic data.json (e.g. 300 tasks) as a secondary, loosely-bounded check.
  *Empirical grounding:* a Codex probe parsed the real codexu `data.json` (180 tasks) in ~7ms median
  / 10ms max over 20 runs — the lifecycle read is ~3 orders of magnitude under the 1s budget, which
  disconfirms the brainstorm's "not sub-second" disproof.
- **`task-aliases.mjs` has no `.d.mts`.** Importing `resolveTaskLifecycle` from the TS package would
  fail `npm run typecheck`. Primary path avoids the import (direct normalized `task.lifecycle` read);
  if used, add `scripts/lib/task-aliases.d.mts` in the same story (see D-C).
- **Enrichment field naming / consumer expectations.** `enrichment` is additive; confirm no
  downstream consumer asserts an exact `ReadyTask` key set and no docs/snapshot fixture pins the
  result shape. Update the tool `description` so agents understand the lifecycle-authoritative contract.
- **Marketplace-index + version-table consistency.** plugin.json + 3 toolkit-root indexes + root
  codexu `AGENTS.md` Active Plugin Versions table must all read 2.10.0; the codex index
  (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`) policy enums must stay valid (run
  `node tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs` from the toolkit root). Submodule two-commit flow
  must be followed (see Repo & Submodule Workflow).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 (merged/archived exclusion, tested invariant):** Given a fixture where `data.json` marks N
  snapshot-ready-staged tasks as `merged`/`archived` and the snapshot is NOT re-synced,
  `overview.parallel_ready_tasks` returns **zero** of those N tasks. Verified by a new test asserting
  none of the merged/archived ids appear in `taskIds(result)`.
- **AC2 (same-day filing inclusion):** Given `data.json` containing a new `tracked` task absent from
  `snapshot.json`, the tool returns that task with a non-null kickoff `command` (derived from
  `initialStage` + `command.prompts`) and `enrichment === 'awaiting-sync'`. Verified by a new test.
- **AC3 (staleness surfacing):** When `snapshot.json` mtime is older than `data.json` mtime, the
  result includes a numeric `snapshotAgeMs` and a non-empty `snapshotStaleReason` whose text both
  includes the age and identifies the cause as `data.json newer than snapshot` (distinct from the
  AC6 snapshot-missing wording). Verified via a `setMtime()`-based test that asserts the numeric age
  and a stable substring for the data-newer case.
- **AC4 (lifecycle-aware prerequisite):** A `tracked` dependent whose only blocker is `merged` in
  data.json is returned as actionable even when the blocker's snapshot stage is stale (≠ `shipped`).
  Verified by a new test.
- **AC5 (blockedOn honored for snapshot-absent task):** A snapshot-absent `tracked` task with
  `blockedOn:[X]` where X's lifecycle ≠ `merged` is NOT actionable; flipping X to `merged` makes it
  actionable. Verified by a new test.
- **AC6 (graceful missing snapshot):** With `data.json` present and `snapshot.json` absent, the tool
  returns `ok:true` with data.json-driven candidates all marked `enrichment:'awaiting-sync'`,
  `snapshotAgeMs === null`, and a snapshot-missing `snapshotStaleReason`. Verified by a new test.
- **AC7 (no regressions):** The full existing `parallel-ready-tasks.test.ts` (dependency + story
  gating + curator-conflict + watcher-failure cases) passes unchanged (fixtures may gain explicit
  blocker lifecycle but assertions are unchanged).
- **AC8 (freshness without watcher):** A **direct `snapshot-reader.test.ts` test** (the helper is
  shared by `expand-task-context`, so it must be covered at the reader level, not only via the tool):
  after `getOverviewData()` is first read, mutating `data.json` and advancing its mtime via
  `setMtime()` and calling `getOverviewData()` again returns the new lifecycle WITHOUT calling
  `reader.start()`. A tool-level assertion of the same effect may be added but does not replace the
  reader-level test.
- **AC9 (performance / no full sync):** The read path parses `data.json` at most once per call and
  performs no job-state walk beyond the existing `computeSnapshotStaleSince` mtime stats. Verified
  with a **concrete instrumentation seam** — e.g. a spy/mock around the data-loader
  (`loadOverviewData`) asserting call-count ≤ 1, or a test-only parse counter on `SnapshotReader` —
  NOT by timing alone. A secondary, loosely-bounded timer over a 300-task synthetic fixture (well
  under 1s) is informational only.
- **AC10 (version + docs):** Performed via `/release-plugin` (or mirroring its outputs):
  `plugin.json` and all three TOOLKIT-root marketplace indexes report `2.10.0`; `CHANGELOG.md` has a
  2.10.0 entry; the root codexu `AGENTS.md` Active Plugin Versions table reads `ralph-overview 2.10.0`;
  `node tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs` (run from the toolkit root) passes; this plugin's
  `AGENTS.md` documents the lifecycle-first read + staleness fields; the submodule two-commit flow is
  followed and all commits are LOCAL (no push/release without lead/operator approval — ask before push).
- **AC11 (typecheck/build):** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` (overview-mcp workspace) pass;
  `npm test` is green.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001** — Lifecycle-first authoritative candidate construction (merge helper: data.json base +
  overlay `ralph`/`unblockCandidate`), hard `merged`/`archived` exclusion, `isCandidateStage` over
  merged tasks, single-parse `loadPrdsByTaskId({overviewData})`, + mtime-guarded `getOverviewData()`.
  (AC1, AC8, partial AC11)
- **US-002** — Authoritative readiness + same-day-filing inclusion: freshly-derived dependency graph
  (`deriveDependencyGraph` over data.json + PRDs; `blockedOn` + reverse `blocks`), lifecycle-aware
  prerequisite satisfaction, `enrichment` marker, `deriveNextCommand` kickoff, **graceful
  missing-snapshot**. (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7)
- **US-003** — Staleness surfacing (`snapshotAgeMs: number | null` + `snapshotStaleReason`) + tool
  `description` update + performance/no-full-sync instrumentation. (AC3, AC9)
- **US-004** — Version bump to 2.10.0 via `/release-plugin` (plugin.json + 3 toolkit-root marketplace
  indexes + CHANGELOG + codex policy validation; defer the push/release step to the lead) + plugin
  `AGENTS.md` docs + root codexu `AGENTS.md` Active Plugin Versions table + submodule pointer commit.
  Commit locally; ask before any push. (AC10)

(Full per-story acceptance criteria in `stories-outline.md`.)

## Suggested Decomposition

All functional stories (US-001..US-003) edit the **same file**
(`tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/parallel-ready-tasks.ts`) and its single test file, so they have
maximal file overlap and MUST run **serially**. US-004 (version/docs) touches disjoint files but is
logically last (it documents the shipped behavior). A single serial cluster is recommended;
parallelization offers no benefit for this single-surface change.

### Cluster: lifecycle-first-read
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/parallel-ready-tasks.ts`,
  `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/parallel-ready-tasks.test.ts`]; exclusive (US-004)=[`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
  marketplace indexes, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`]; risk=high (US-001..003 same file)
- `execution_mode` rationale: US-001..US-003 mutate the same function bodies in one file and the
  same test file; running them in parallel would guarantee merge conflicts, so they are serialized
  in a single cluster. US-004 is appended to the same serial cluster because it documents the final
  behavior and is trivially fast.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json`

## Open Questions
- **Enrichment field name.** `enrichment: 'synced' | 'awaiting-sync'` vs `stageSource: 'snapshot' |
  'data.json'`. Plan picks `enrichment`; the implementer may rename if a clearer convention exists,
  as long as it is additive and documented in AGENTS.md.
- **`snapshotStaleReason` wording.** Exact human string is left to the implementer; it must name the
  age and the cause (data.json newer / snapshot missing).
- **Whether to fold US-004 docs into US-003.** Kept separate so a docs-only failure does not block
  the behavioral stories; the implementer may merge them if running serially in one job.
